item.title: D.L. Hughley Obliterates Stephen A. Smith Over Trump Dinner And Questions His Loyalty To Black America
item.dc:creator: Houston Williams
item.description: GAT DAMN, DL! D.L. Hughley just gave Stephen A. Smith a lesson in Black accountability, and the outspoken sports commentator may have underestimated the comedian’s willingness to fight back. DL made it clear, he’s not a regular comedian. He stands on business. The feud has become increasingly personal since Smith attended a White House dinner …
item.content:encoded:
GAT DAMN, DL!

D.L. Hughley just gave Stephen A. Smith a lesson in Black accountability, and the outspoken sports commentator may have underestimated the comedian’s willingness to fight back. DL made it clear, he’s not a regular comedian. He stands on business.

The feud has become increasingly personal since Smith attended a White House dinner with President Donald Trump, Bill Maher and Kid Rock. Hughley questioned the political implications of that gathering, and Smith responded by challenging what Hughley had ever accomplished for Black people. Wrong thing to say.

Well, sometimes you ask a question and get an answer you really didn’t want.

During the “GED Section” of “The D.L. Hughley Show,” the veteran comedian delivered a meticulous response that sounded less like a comedy routine and more like a courtroom closing argument. 

Hughley began by discussing his books, including How Not to Get Shot, How to Survive America, Surrender, White People! and Black Man, White House. He also highlighted his Peabody Award winning documentary The Endangered List.

“Every book I’ve ever written was to highlight the injustices leveled at Black people,” Hughley said.

He wasn’t finished.

Hughley recalled performing benefit shows for Flint residents during their water crisis, raising scholarship funds in Chicago and helping families affected by the racist Buffalo supermarket massacre. He also cited charitable efforts following the Altadena wildfires and Charleston church shooting.

Then came the White House business.

Smith had previously mocked Hughley’s access to the White House, apparently unaware that the comedian had already visited during previous administrations. Hughley pointed out another distinction: Smith attended Trump’s dinner as Maher’s guest.

“When I stepped off, you stepped in,” Hughley said, referencing his own decision to distance himself from Maher over the television host’s racial commentary.

That’s where the disagreement became particularly uncomfortable.

Hughley challenged Smith’s justification that the presidential gathering concerned historically Black colleges and universities. He characterized the administration’s $500 million HBCU funding commitment as financial maneuvering rather than genuinely new investment.

“He robbed DeAndre to pay Malik,” Hughley declared.

That assessment is Hughley’s characterization of the funding decision, not an independently established accounting conclusion. He contrasted the administration’s figure with the approximately $17 billion in HBCU support credited to former President Joe Biden. September 16, 2024

Ultimately, Hughley questioned whether political access means much when the community supposedly being represented receives no demonstrable benefit.

“What does it profit a man to gain the world and lose his soul?” he asked.

He finished with a challenge that may sting longer than any insult.

“I do my very best. Can you say the same?”

Will S.A. Smith will respond?

item.title: Rick Ross Son Taking Online Courses After Being Pistol-Whipped On Campus
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Tia Kemp says her son is bouncing back after the violent attack near Bethune-Cookman University left him shaken but determined to move forward with his education. William Roberts III was struck with a handgun on October 11 when a 20-year-old man confronted him over a woman, but the family’s response has shifted focus entirely toward …
item.content:encoded:
Tia Kemp says her son is bouncing back after the violent attack near Bethune-Cookman University left him shaken but determined to move forward with his education.

William Roberts III was struck with a handgun on October 11 when a 20-year-old man confronted him over a woman, but the family’s response has shifted focus entirely toward institutional accountability rather than the individual assault.

“He’s pursuing his masters online,” Kemp explained in a recent interview, emphasizing how quickly she pulled her son from campus after the incident. “I definitely got him back home and he’s pursuing his masters online. They was able to give him his classes online. He would not step foot back over.”

The university accommodated the transition, allowing William to continue his graduate studies remotely while the family processes what happened.

Kemp’s legal strategy isn’t aimed at the alleged attacker or even the public figures inserting themselves into the situation. She holds the city of Daytona and Bethune-Cookman University directly responsible for what she sees as a massive security failure.

“The city of Daytona with Cookman University. Yeah, we are coming. Cuz that’s a major security issue,” Kemp stated firmly, making her position crystal clear about where accountability lies.

When asked whether the conflict would ever reach resolution, Kemp’s response was unambiguous.

item.title: Paul Pierce Claims TV Pay Loss Strained His Finances
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Paul Pierce said his finances suffered after Fox Sports checks stopped as his custody fight with Princess Santiago continued.
item.content:encoded:
Paul Pierce said his lost TV income left him struggling with support bills in his custody fight with former girlfriend Princess Santiago.

TMZ said Pierce listed $300,000 in cash, $3 million in property, $23,000 in business income last month and $48,000 in monthly bills.

He claimed $48,000 in monthly support and opposed $40,000 for Santiago’s lawyers plus $10,000 for an accountant, TMZ reported separately.

Pierce listed earlier monthly income of $119,000 and said his final Fox Sports payment arrived in August, PEOPLE reported.

“Having lost his Fox Sports contract, while simultaneously facing these substantial financial obligations, Respondent is drowning financially,” his lawyer wrote.

EssentiallySports reported that Pierce posted “Cap” on X amid the reports, without explaining which financial figure he disputed.

The money fight followed competing custody requests for their infant son, King Rafael Santiago Pierce. Us Weekly reviewed the court documents in April in which Pierce acknowledged paternity and sought joint custody of the baby. Santiago had asked for sole legal and physical custody, along with $29,811 each month in child support.

She also sought $100,000 for legal fees and close to $19,000 in pregnancy-related costs. Santiago, an event director in Los Angeles, argued that Pierce’s endorsement money had once covered his spending without him needing to touch his NBA salary. Her filing pointed to his own public description of those earnings to support her request. She put his career NBA salary alone at between $195 million and $203 million.

She sought health insurance for King at Pierce’s expense.

His television work had changed well before the latest financial filing. Fox Sports canceled “Speak,” the show on which Pierce appeared, in July 2025. Front Office Sports confirmed that the cuts also took out “Breakfast Ball” and “The Facility.” Three of the network’s five daily shows ended in that shake-up.

Santiago had first sought a DNA test in January, saying she had tried to settle the matter privately. She later said she went through the pregnancy without financial help or an in-person visit from Pierce. By April, the court filings showed he was seeking a shared role in raising King.

item.title: Cardi B Says Her Inner Circle’s Resentment Is Making Her Evil & Dangerous
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Cardi B describes growing distrust within her inner circle and explains why she wants distance from people as her career hits new heights.
item.content:encoded:
Cardi B just revealed something most people never want to admit out loud: success has a price that money can’t fix.

During a recent live stream, the 34-year-old rapper got real about how reaching the top has isolated her from the people she thought she could trust, and the jealousy she’s experiencing from her inner circle is reshaping who she is as a person.

The Bronx native didn’t hold back when describing what it feels like to achieve at her level.

“It’s so crazy that at the age of 34, I’m still learning lessons. I’m still taking L’s and I’m still learning lessons,” she explained, adding that success has put her in a position where she’s constantly discovering new betrayals.

The hardest part isn’t the fame itself, it’s realizing that the people closest to her resent her wins instead of celebrating them.

“I’m experiencing jealousy and I’m experiencing people trying to humble me the most,” Cardi B said, making it clear that this isn’t coming from random haters online.

It’s coming from her circle. She described how impossible it’s become to share good news without triggering resentment from those she cares about.

“Being successful, it is so scary. You just don’t know who got that secret animosity for you,” she continued. “It’s like you cannot even express, hey, I got a new contract because deep down they’re upset that you getting it.”

The toll this has taken on her personality is real. Cardi B said she used to be nice and kind, but the constant attempts to tear her down have made her feel like she’s becoming someone colder and meaner.

She’s reached the highest point of her career and life, but that achievement has come with a loneliness that’s almost unbearable.

“It’s lonely at the top. I have never been as high as I am right now in my career, in my everything. And it just makes me want to be alone for real,” she said. “I want to change my number and just go away. Y’all turning me so evil and so dangerous.”

Cardi B’s comments about dealing with fake friends and secret resentment have resonated with people who understand that success can be isolating.

The rapper’s willingness to discuss these struggles shows a side of fame that rarely gets discussed in interviews.

Fresh off a $70 million tour and celebrating her achievements, Cardi B is grappling with the reality that reaching the top means losing the connections that once grounded her.

item.title: Malcolm Spellman Plans “The Drop”‘s Future
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Malcolm Spellman outlined his vision for "The Drop" and its family's music business fight as FX's renewal decision remained open.
item.content:encoded:
Malcolm Spellman wants record-label power to drive the next chapter of “The Drop: A Snowfall Saga”, with the show’s family caught in the squeeze.

In an interview with The Hollywood Reporter, he described plans for seasons two and three. FX has not renewed the series, and Spellman said he had heard nothing from the network about another season.

He saw season one as an introduction to the family, with its final episodes leaning into the music business.

“The music business destroys families, and this family will spend its entire existence in this show trying to survive,” he said.

The drama takes place in 1990s Los Angeles, after “Snowfall” followed the city’s crack epidemic. Gail Bean returned as Wanda Bell, while Isaiah John reprised Leon Simmons. Wanda’s pursuit of a place in rap runs alongside Leon’s work serving the community through a legal clinic.

That shift gave Wanda a different kind of power. In the original series, she struggled with addiction, entered recovery and left for Ghana with Leon. In the spinoff, she builds a team around her own ambition rather than living at the mercy of Franklin Saint’s operation.

Music also runs through the family itself. Asante Blackk plays Wanda’s younger cousin Lamar Kinsey, whose gift she has encouraged for years. Peyton Alex Smith plays Lamar’s older brother James, who faces pressure from Big Daddy to take over the family business.

Artillery, played by Compton rapper Buddy, brings another set of problems. FX describes the character as a gifted writer facing both street recognition and hostility from the LAPD’s CRASH unit. His songs put him in conflict with forces beyond the recording booth.

Buddy had already connected the role to his own experience during an NABJ conversation covered by AllHipHop. He described signing away intellectual property and seeing label-approved budgets turn into costs he would owe later. That was the business experience he brought to a fictional rapper trying to find his way.

At the NABJ preview, Bean pointed to Wanda’s family and her relationship with Leon as parts of the new story. John described returning to Leon as a chance to keep building the character’s arc.

Spellman’s next chapter would examine label manipulation alongside the pressure that money and gangs put on the family.

item.title: A$AP Rocky AI Video Theft Claim Draws Measured Response From Jason Paul
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: A$AP Rocky's "Shroom Clouds" dispute drew a response from Jason Paul, who weighed his options without blaming the rapper.
item.content:encoded:
A$AP Rocky got a measured response from Jason Paul amid the dispute over “Shroom Clouds.” The parkour athlete said he was weighing his options but did not put the blame on the rapper.

“I’m not mad at ASAP Rocky. I love the dude’s music,” Paul said.

He doubted the label was to blame, saying its staff could not know every Instagram clip. He made the 2019 footage with visual artists Cache Bunny and Ari Fararooy.

The allegations previously covered by AllHipHop centered on a short sequence in the new music video. Cache Bunny accused the production of using the older work without permission.

The earlier project featured Paul moving through a landscape turned into a tunnel. Cache Bunny alleged that AI replaced Paul with Rocky while keeping the original setting.

The production’s credits included AI artists Spike and Red, along with Ces. Those roles alone did not establish who handled the disputed scene. Rocky shared directing credit with Aisultan Seitov and Pietro Biz Biasia.

The video also featured a mural of A$AP Yams and a callback to Rocky’s “Purple Swag,” placing the disputed segment among references to his own career.

Cache Bunny also questioned why the team had not asked to license the footage or created its own version of the idea. The artist said she was unsure how to proceed.

“Shroom Clouds” featured reggie and Jeremih, with production from Sleeping Bear and Hector Delgado. The song had been performed years before its release and was previously known as “Mushroom Clouds.”

Visual work has been a major part of Rocky’s career beyond records.

In June, he accepted Tribeca X’s first Filmmaker of the Year Award. The honor recognized work across music, fashion, film and brand storytelling. During his acceptance speech, Rocky described music videos as a way to express his past and experiences.

Paul also said he contacted a “Shroom Clouds” director, who told him the video had been shot five years earlier and was “out of my hands,” PetaPixel reported. The report did not name that director.

item.title: Tyga Sued For Bailing On Two Concerts In Taiwan & Keeping The Loot
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Tyga faced a $135,000 Beijing lawsuit after alleged missed appearances, failed rescheduling and disputed refund arrangements.
item.content:encoded:
Tyga is facing a fraud and breach-of-contract suit from Beijing Tongxing Wanxin Catering Management for ditching two shows, TMZ reported.

The company alleged the rapper missed Club Pac Star appearances on August 4 and October 27, 2023. He was supposed to perform in the first half of 2024 and sent a $10,000 settlement refund of the $145,000 he was paid.

But the company never received the remaining $135,000, and it wants it back, plus interest and punitive damages.

Local consumer officials previously scrutinized Tyga over the canceled Taiwan booking. In a March 20, 2025 statement, Taipei’s Department of Legal Affairs said it had received 52 complaints from consumers who said they had not received refunds.

That booking covered a November 21, 2024 show at Zepp New Taipei and an after-party at OMNI in Taipei.

The department identified Onion Production as the overseas promoter. Local firms arranged Tyga’s work permit and rented the performance venue.

Officials said the company did not attend their administrative inquiry and had been asked, through a local company, to publish more details about refunds and rescheduling.

The promoter posted an update on its event page. A November 20, 2024 notice blamed an unforeseen personal matter involving the artist for the cancellations. It said the company was working with his team to find another date.

In a March 20, 2025 update, Onion Production said refunds had started in mid-January. It attributed some delays to verification requirements under Taiwan’s anti-money laundering rules and said it had transferred funds to ticketing platform Eventix.

According to the promoter, Eventix was processing refunds through the original payment method.

item.title: Trial In Project Pat’s Son’s Killing Pushed Back To December
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Project Pat's son's murder case received a December 9 trial date as two women faced charges in the 2025 Memphis killing.
item.content:encoded:
The trial in the killing of Project Pat‘s son has been pushed back to December 9, according to Action News 5.

Talia Jones and Jermiesia Franklin face charges in the death of Patrick Houston Jr., who was 21 when he was killed in Memphis. Jones had previously been scheduled to go to trial on September 21.

Jones is charged with facilitation of first-degree murder. Franklin was indicted on two counts of first-degree murder, aggravated robbery and tampering with or fabricating evidence. Prosecutors accused Franklin of shooting Houston and taking his cellphone. Her case was placed in adult court. She was being held on a $5 million bond when the indictment was reported in September. Franklin was 18 at the time of the September report and had been 16 when Houston was killed.

The charges against the women followed a fatal shooting on January 10, 2025. Houston was killed near Ketchum Road and Long Street in Memphis, according to the U.S. Marshals Service. Memphis police investigated the killing before Jones was sought on a warrant issued June 27, 2025.

Federal marshals later tracked Jones to Minnesota. The agency’s Two Rivers Violent Fugitive Task Force took on the case and developed leads that she had left Tennessee. Marshals arrested her in Minneapolis on July 15, 2025.

The Marshals Service said Jones fought and resisted during the arrest. Agents subdued her without anyone being injured, according to the agency. She was then held in Minnesota while awaiting extradition to Tennessee.

Houston shared his father’s name. Project Pat, born Patrick Houston Sr., is Juicy J’s older brother and a longtime figure in Memphis Hip-Hop. He delivered the hook on Three 6 Mafia’s 2000 song “Sippin’ on Some Syrup” and later appeared on Drake’s “Knife Talk,” from the 2021 album Certified Lover Boy.

Outside music, the rapper started the Go Foundation in 2021 and has visited prisons as part of his ministry work. His outreach has included the weekly Breakin’ Baggs ministry at 201 Poplar in Memphis. In an AllHipHop interview, he explained that he was a minister and preacher, though he was not an ordained pastor.

item.title: BigXthaPlug Gives Dallas Fans First Listen to ‘Better Over Time’
item.dc:creator: Crystal Willis
item.description: BigXthaPlug gave AllHipHop an exclusive preview of his new album, Better Over Time, ahead of its October 30 release.
item.content:encoded:
Dallas-based scribe Crystal Willis gives insights on BigX’s star-studded new album and accompanying short film.

Dallas showed up for one of its own Monday night as multi-platinum rapper BigXthaPlug gave fans an exclusive first listen to his upcoming album, Better Over Time, during a private listening event and short film screening on October 26.

Held at a Cinemark theater in Dallas, the event offered invited guests an early look at the rapper’s latest creative chapter, combining new music with a cinematic experience just days before the project’s official October 30 release.

But the experience didn’t end inside the theater. Following the screening, BigXthaPlug surprised fans with an impromptu parking lot performance filmed for an upcoming YouTube show. Fans were invited to make a cameo during the taping, giving AllHipHop a behind-the-scenes look at the unexpected moment as the Dallas rapper brought his energy directly to the crowd.

The hometown screening was part of a multi-city promotional rollout that included Charlotte, North Carolina, on October 26, followed by Houston, Miami and Los Angeles on October 27.

BigXthaPlug Brings Star Power to ‘Better Over Time’

Better Over Time boasts an impressive lineup of collaborators, including Lil Yachty, GloRilla, Leon Thomas, Loe Shimmy, Babyface Ray, Fridayy, Ava Max, Ro$ama and Belly Gang Kushington.

The project follows BigXthaPlug’s country-inspired album I Hope You’re Happy, which expanded his audience beyond traditional Hip-Hop and debuted at No. 7 on the Billboard 200.

With Better Over Time, X continues building on his success while exploring themes of growth, ambition and the realities that come with navigating fame. The accompanying short film adds another dimension to the project, extending the album’s storytelling beyond the recording studio and onto the screen.

The exclusive screenings also reflect an increasingly popular approach to album promotion, where artists create immersive experiences that give fans more than a traditional listening party.

For BigXthaPlug, combining new music, film and an unexpected live performance provided an opportunity to connect with his audience ahead of the highly anticipated release.

From Dallas Roots to Mainstream Success

BigXthaPlug’s rise has been fueled by his commanding delivery, unmistakable Texas sound and unapologetic approach to storytelling. Breakout records including “Texas,” “Mmhmm” and “Levels” helped establish his presence in Hip-Hop, while his 2024 sophomore album Take Care debuted at No. 8 on the Billboard 200.

His momentum continued with sold-out tour dates, major festival appearances and growing industry recognition. His Take Care North American Tour sold out 30 venues and drew more than 35,000 fans, further demonstrating his expanding reach.

More recently, his collaboration with country artist Bailey Zimmerman, “All The Way,” reached No. 1 on Billboard’s Hot Country Songs chart, highlighting his ability to connect with audiences across genres without abandoning his Texas roots.

Despite his mainstream success, Dallas remains central to BigXthaPlug’s identity. Hosting an exclusive listening experience in his hometown gave local supporters an opportunity to celebrate his latest milestone before the music reaches a global audience.

With a star-studded tracklist, cinematic rollout and another major release on the horizon, BigXthaPlug continues to establish himself as one of the most compelling voices emerging from Texas Hip-Hop.

Better Over Time arrives Friday, October 30, on major streaming platforms.

item.title: Ice Cube’s “Last Friday” Gets Director As Movie Production Ramps Up
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Ice Cube's "Last Friday" tapped Lawrence Lamont, bringing the Detroit filmmaker's Hip-Hop background to the comedy franchise.
item.content:encoded:
Ice Cube‘s “Last Friday” named Lawrence Lamont its director, according to The Hollywood Reporter.

The filmmaker already has a comedy with Keke Palmer and SZA under his belt. He directed “One Of Them Days,” written by Syreeta Singleton and produced by a team that included Issa Rae and Deniese Davis. Its cast also included Katt Williams, Lil Rel Howery and Janelle James.

Lamont’s ties to Hip-Hop go well beyond that movie. Raised in Detroit, he built a body of work that includes videos for Big Sean and J. Cole. His own portfolio lists Sean’s “Single Again” and Cole’s “GOMD,” plus work with Sean and Jhené Aiko’s duo Twenty88. He also directed Snoop Dogg in a Menulog commercial.

Television brought another connection to Rae: “Rap Sh!t.” Lamont’s portfolio lists work on both seasons of the series. In a 2022 interview with Little Black Book, he described music videos as a place to develop storytelling skills while working with tight budgets and just a few minutes of screen time.

“One Of Them Days” gave him room to tell a longer story, with Palmer and SZA playing friends trying to avoid eviction after their rent money disappears. The comedy earned more than $50 million worldwide. TheWrap reported in June 2025 that TriStar was developing a sequel, with Lamont, Singleton, Palmer and SZA expected back at that stage.

For Cube, the director news followed two updates about getting “Last Friday” made. He told fans in Long Beach on July 17 that he and Mike Epps had turned in the script. The pair appeared together at a celebration of the films.

Then California announced on October 7 that New Line’s “Last Friday” was among 35 films awarded state production tax credits. The California Film Commission identified Cube as the movie’s star, writer and producer.

“I’m thrilled to produce Last Friday right here in Southern California, where our cast and crew lives,” Cube said in the state announcement.

He said the production planned to employ more than 180 local cast and crew members. Cube also pointed to the story’s roots in South Los Angeles, dating back to the first movie 31 years earlier.
